detail.title: Administrative Justice and the Boards of Appeal of EU Agencies
detail.abstract:
This book provides the first comprehensive analysis of EU Boards of Appeal—specialized review bodies within European agencies processing thousands of decisions annually across trademark protection (EUIPO), chemical safety (ECHA), aviation (EASA), financial supervision (ESAs), energy (ACER), and other domains.

The study examines Boards' constitutional foundations, empirical performance, and institutional challenges through doctrinal analysis, data from the University of Ferrara Common Database, and comparison with UK, French, German, and US systems.

Three fundamental questions structure the inquiry. First, what is Boards' legal nature? They constitute sui generis hybrids combining administrative expertise with quasi-judicial procedures. Second, do Boards satisfy Article 47 Charter requirements? Generally yes, though independence from parent agencies remains problematic. The Article 58a filter limiting Court of Justice access (1-2% admission rate) raises constitutional concerns. Third, what review standard applies? Aquind (2018) mandated "full review," causing the empirically documented "Aquind Spike"—18% increase in processing times.

Empirical assessment through 2025 shows strong performance: 6-12 month processing versus judicial 24+ months, 55-70% confirmation rates indicating balanced review, 75-85% judicial confirmation validating quality. Substantive contributions include EUIPO's NFT/metaverse doctrine (2024-2025), ECHA's PFAS jurisprudence (2025), ACER's hydrogen regulation (2024), and cross-Board AI evidence standards.

Comparative analysis reveals critical findings. Transatlantic convergence: EU's Aquind (2018) and US Loper Bright (2024) both rejected administrative deference within six years. Yet divergence persists as US questions administrative adjudication (Jarkesy) while EU consolidates it. Spanish perspective reveals institutional gaps—no specialized tribunals, only direct judicial review.

Three existential reforms emerge. "Ring-fenced Fee Model" provides budgetary independence. "Regulation on Administrative Procedure for Union Bodies" (2028) eliminates arbitrary variations. "Common Protocol on Algorithmic Adjudication" addresses the Aquind-AI Paradox: full review mandates colliding with opaque AI governance.

Writing in January 2026, Boards face decisive challenges. When ECHA reviews toxicity, EASA evaluates safety, ESAs assess stability, administrative justice quality becomes literally life and death. Success requires evolution toward coherence, independence, and technological capability.

 KEYWORDS: EU administrative law, Boards of Appeal, EUIPO, ECHA, Article 47, Aquind, Article 58a, AI governance, Loper Bright

title: A Comparative Analysis of Stablecoin Interest Prohibition Under MiCA and the GENIUS Act
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: A Comparative Analysis of Stablecoin Interest Prohibition Under MiCA and the GENIUS Act
detail.abstract: The prohibition of interest-bearing stablecoins marks a critical juncture in digital asset regulation, exposing fundamental tensions between financial innovation and systemic stability. This paper provides the first comparative legal and financial analysis of the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) and the United States' GENIUS Act of 2025, examining how two major jurisdictions reach convergent prohibitions on yield-bearing stablecoins through markedly divergent regulatory architectures. While both frameworks forbid direct interest payments to holders, they diverge sharply in their treatment of decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, reserve composition requirements, and supervisory allocation. The paper advances three interconnected contributions: (1) a technical examination of reserve management mechanisms and their implications for run dynamics; (2) a scenario-based stress test identifying contagion pathways from stablecoin markets to traditional banking systems; and (3) an analysis of the "DeFi gap," the substantial regulatory perimeter failure whereby third-party protocols offer functionally equivalent yields outside statutory prohibitions. With stablecoin market capitalization exceeding $300 billion, rivaling the deposit bases of mid-sized national banking systems-the regulatory treatment of these instruments will determine whether they evolve as competitors to traditional banks or as complementary infrastructure within a restructured financial system.

title: Institutional Crypto Asset Integration in U.S. Pension Funds and University Endowments: Evidence from SEC 13F Filings, Q1 2024 through Q4 2025
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Institutional Crypto Asset Integration in U.S. Pension Funds and University Endowments: Evidence from SEC 13F Filings, Q1 2024 through Q4 2025
detail.abstract: The January 10, 2024 approval of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission created the first regulated, operationally accessible vehicle for institutional investors to obtain direct Bitcoin price exposure through conventional brokerage infrastructure. This study provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of institutional crypto asset adoption in the two years following that regulatory turning point, examining quarterly SEC Form 13F-HR filings for a sample of 20 major institutional investors comprising 15 U.S. public pension funds and 5 university endowments across eight quarters from Q1 2024 through Q4 2025. Aggregate institutional crypto asset holdings grew from $450,216,676 at the Q1 2024 baseline to a peak of $1,478,823,205 in Q3 2025, before declining 34.7% to $965,495,831 in Q4 2025. Three findings carry first-order significance for researchers and policymakers. First, pension funds and university endowments pursued categorically distinct investment vehicle strategies throughout the study period: pension funds concentrated in MicroStrategy equity (MSTR) as a leveraged Bitcoin proxy, with MSTR representing up to 58.4% of aggregate pension holdings, while endowments held exclusively in spot ETFs. This vehicle bifurcation produced a 24.2 percentage-point performance differential during the Q4 2025 drawdown, with pension funds declining 43.0% versus endowments declining 18.8%. Second, share-count decomposition reveals heterogeneous institutional behavior, with 18 instances of active accumulation and 23 of deliberate reduction during Q4 2025, confirming that institutional crypto allocation involves active portfolio management rather than passive price exposure. Third, Harvard Management Company's Q4 2025 simultaneous reduction of iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) and initiation of a $86.8 million iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) position represents the first major intra-crypto portfolio rotation in the sample and may foreshadow broader multi-asset institutional crypto adoption. The results advance understanding of how large fiduciaries navigate novel asset classes under conditions of regulatory ambiguity and investment policy constraint.

title: Institutional Crypto Asset Integration: Fiduciary Prudence and the Price of Product Choice
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Institutional Crypto Asset Integration: Fiduciary Prudence and the Price of Product Choice
detail.abstract: The January 2024 regulatory approval of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) created the first regulated, operationally accessible vehicle for institutional fiduciaries to obtain direct Bitcoin price exposure. This article examines the two-year period following that transition, drawing on SEC Form 13F filings from 15 public pension funds and five university endowments. While aggregate institutional crypto holdings reached a peak of $1.48 billion in late 2025, a subsequent market correction revealed a stark performance differential between institution types. The gap between pension funds (-43.0%) and endowments (-18.8%) traces directly to a single governance decision: the choice of investment vehicle. This article documents that divergence and draws practical implications for fiduciaries, investment committee members, and board trustees.

title: Stablecoins vs. Traditional P2P Payment Systems: A Critical Analysis of the Push for U.S. Retail Adoption
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Stablecoins vs. Traditional P2P Payment Systems: A Critical Analysis of the Push for U.S. Retail Adoption
detail.abstract: The passage of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act in July 2025 and subsequent state-level initiatives have positioned stablecoins for potentially significant integration into the U.S. financial system. Proponents frame these developments as financial innovation and evidence of American technological leadership. This paper critically examines a fundamental question: why would a U.S. consumer need a stablecoin for retail transactions when established peer-to-peer payment systems such as Venmo, PayPal, and Zelle already provide secure, instantaneous, and widely accepted digital payment services? Drawing on a mixed-methods approach that incorporates market data, legislative analysis, documented campaign finance activity, and comparative case studies, this paper argues that the push for stablecoin adoption in U.S. retail payments lacks a compelling consumer-centric rationale. The genuine advantages of stablecoins, including lower cross-border transaction costs, inflation hedging in economies with unstable currencies, and institutional efficiency gains, are largely irrelevant to the average U.S. consumer. Instead, the momentum behind stablecoin adoption appears to be driven by two interrelated forces: concentrated industry interests seeking regulatory capture, evidenced by substantial and documented political spending, and political dynamics in which support for financial innovation serves as a mechanism for alignment with influential stakeholders and the broader pursuit of U.S. digital finance leadership. The paper concludes that policymakers should prioritize consumer protection over industry rents and that U.S. consumers currently have limited reason to substitute existing P2P systems with stablecoins.

title: When States Buy Bitcoin: Political Signaling, Fiscal Risk, and the Empirical Failure of Strategic Cryptocurrency Reserves
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: When States Buy Bitcoin: Political Signaling, Fiscal Risk, and the Empirical Failure of Strategic Cryptocurrency Reserves
detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive empirical and theoretical critique of proposals to establish state-level Bitcoin strategic reserves. Using Missouri House Bill 2080 as a contemporary case study, the author analyzes the performance of $10 million hypothetical investments in Bitcoin, gold (GLD ETF), and 3-month Treasury bills across five strategic investment dates during 2025 and 2026. The results are consistent across all scenarios: Bitcoin investments lost an average of 30.5% of principal, gold gained an average of 51.1%, and Treasury bills preserved capital with modest positive returns, Risk metrics reveal Bitcoin's annualized volatility of 43.92%, nearly double gold's 24.40% and more than 100 times Treasury bills' annualized volatility of 0.41%, with a 95% Value at Risk of $461,371 per day for a $10 million position. Drawing on event study evidence from Texas's $5 million Bitcoin purchase, which generated statistically insignificant market reactions, this paper argues that state-level cryptocurrency reserves represent political signaling rather than sound fiscal management. The paper contributes to public finance theory by identifying the "libertarian-state paradox," whereby governments adopting an explicitly anti-state technology undermine both the technology's core principles and their own fiduciary duties. The paper concludes with a template for evaluating future cryptocurrency policy proposals based on scale and market response tests.

title: Why Financial Intelligence Reaches Its Full Potential Through System Literacy
affiliations: New York State Department of Taxation & Finance

detail.title: Why Financial Intelligence Reaches Its Full Potential Through System Literacy
detail.abstract:
Financial intelligence is commonly associated with analytical proficiency, including the ability to interpret data, apply economic reasoning, and navigate regulatory frameworks. However, as financial environments become increasingly complex and system-driven, analytical skill alone is often insufficient to produce consistent, accountable, and resilient outcomes. This paper argues that financial intelligence reaches its full potential only when it is supported by system literacy—the ability to understand how decisions are operationalized within interconnected institutional, procedural, and technological systems.

Drawing on interdisciplinary literature from finance, accounting, organizational theory, and governance, this conceptual analysis distinguishes between analytical intelligence and executional intelligence. It demonstrates how system literacy functions as a foundational capability that enables financial insight to translate into effective action. Without an understanding of system design, process dependencies, and institutional constraints, even technically correct financial decisions may fail in practice.

The paper develops a high-level framework illustrating how system awareness enhances decision consistency, accountability, and governance quality. Rather than offering policy prescriptions, the analysis focuses on structural dynamics that shape real-world financial decision-making. The findings have implications for professional education, organizational design, and leadership development, particularly in environments where financial decisions intersect with complex administrative and regulatory systems.

reference: https://www.xinghu.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Credibility-and-Self-preferencing_Xing-SSRN.pdf
title: Invisible Influence: Credibility under Self-Preferencing on Recommendation Platforms

detail.title: Invisible Influence: Credibility under Self-Preferencing on Recommendation Platforms
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Digital platforms now guide most consumption decisions through personalized assortments and ranked recommendations. At the same time, these platforms have strong self-preferencing incentives to push high-margin or strategic content (e.g., originals, sponsored items, private labels). When such incentives are salient, users may no longer treat rankings as neutral advice, but instead question their credibility and adjust their behavior. We study how this tension between platform incentives and user trust shapes engagement, assortment decisions, and long-run platform payoff.

Methodology/results: We develop a game-theoretic model that captures the strategic interactions between a platform and rational users who adjust their beliefs and decide whether to follow, discount, or ignore the recommendations. We introduce platform’s self-preferencing weight toward the high-margin category. Our analysis reveals three distinct equilibrium regimes: compliance, pandering, and zero-compliance. We find that persistent self-preferencing is not always beneficial; excessive bias can lead users to disregard recommendations entirely. Reducing assortment variety can enhance both credibility and profitability, challenging the conventional belief that “more choice is better.” Furthermore, we propose strategies such as donation-match schemes to restore user trust while maintaining profitability.

Managerial implications: Our analysis delivers concise design rules for incentive-driven recommendation systems. When users recognize platform-incentivized options, content curation and ranking should be treated as tools for credibility engineering: sometimes limiting platform-favored items, sometimes softening self-preferencing, and sometimes using donation-match type, value sharing schemes that visibly align the platform’s interests with those of its users and restore trust in the recommendation signal.

title: Organizational Governance and Steward Leadership
affiliations: Columbia International University, Columbia International University

detail.title: Organizational Governance and Steward Leadership
detail.abstract: This analysis provides insights into stewardship within nonprofit governance, particularly regarding the roles of chief stewards or boards of members and under-steward CEOs. Steward Leadership in this context centers on a biblical model, emphasizing non-ownership and accountability to both implicit/explicit owners. The analysis details the governance role of board members, examining the fiduciary, strategic, and potentially generative roles. The examination delves into Chait, Ryan, and Taylor's (2005) explanations of Type I-III governance, including applications of stewardship necessitating flexible organizational structures with oversight. It also includes the overall potential for generative thinking and governance, as well as the board's positioning. This paper highlights the role of the CEO, presenting the dynamics they hold with stakeholders regarding accessibility and public profile, and demonstrating that these must be aligned with the board and that they maintain responsibility for organizational impacts. This analysis concludes with the emphasis that stewardship within governance must focus on flexibility and accountability, noting the respective responsibilities of the chief steward and understeward.

title: From Lists to Oracles: Competition for Generative Search Visibility and Long-Tail Entry

detail.title: From Lists to Oracles: Competition for Generative Search Visibility and Long-Tail Entry
detail.abstract: The transition from ranked-list search engines to generative AI “oracles” represents a fundamental shift in the allocation mechanism of the digital attention economy. We develop a game-theoretic framework to analyze how the move from divisible visibility (lists) to winner-takes-all exclusion (answers) reshapes competitive incentives and market structure. We model the competition between a high-authority Head firm  and a low-authority Tail firm, where the platform’s scoring  rule aggregates prior authority and query-specific evidence via a strategic authority weight, while firms exert costly optimization effort (GEO) to signal their intrinsic relevance. Our results demonstrate that Generative Search drives a surge-or-retreat equilibrium leading to a bifurcated market: in broad queries with commoditized relevance, the game intensifies Matthew-Effect concentration; in niche queries, sufficiently specialized SMEs can overturn incumbency to capture the market via a “long-tail flip.” Furthermore, we uncover a dual-endowment reversal: intrinsic relevance acts as a substitute for effort once a specialist secures the answer slot, whereas an authority disadvantage forces the SME to escalate effort to deter entry. Finally, for platforms and policymakers, we identify the authority weight as a critical market-design lever that dictates competitiveness, redistributes visibility, and determines the quality of information delivered to the user.

reference: https://www.xinghu.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Scrip_System_First_Revision_2026-4-2.pdf
title: Token Design for Favor Trading with Dynamic Membership
affiliations: , The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics and

detail.title: Token Design for Favor Trading with Dynamic Membership
detail.abstract:
This paper investigates the design and management of token-based favor-trading platforms, explicitly accounting for dynamic entry and exit of heterogeneous participants. Favor-trading systems, which facilitate non-monetary reciprocal exchanges, offer substantial potential for resource sharing and collaboration. However, existing research largely assumes a fixed set of participants, limiting its relevance to real-world environments where users frequently join or exit. 

 

To address this gap, we design a dynamic system that accommodates participant turnover and heterogeneity. We propose novel token-based mechanisms: token issuance (at zero balance), redemption (at a finite cap U), and recycling (at exit). Together, they ensure stable token circulation and incentivize an efficient “always-trade” strategy. Our analysis characterizes the conditions for this strategy to prevail in equilibrium, showing it is sustained if the favor's benefit-cost ratio exceeds a specific threshold. Further, we demonstrate that a finite token cap U is necessary for equilibrium and that our recycling mechanism is essential for making the system robust and scalable by preventing the threshold from growing exponentially. We also show the mechanism is robust to participant heterogeneity. 

 

By bridging theoretical insights and practical design, our work provides the first rigorous framework for operating favor-trading systems with dynamic membership. The results have direct implications for time-banking, decentralized capacity-sharing platforms, and broader applications in tokenized service exchanges.

title: Examination of the Theor y of Change Fr amewor k in Str ategy, Policy, and Social Innovation

detail.title: Examination of the Theor y of Change Fr amewor k in Str ategy, Policy, and Social Innovation
detail.abstract: Organizations operating in complex social, economic, and policy environments face a fundamental challenge: demonstrating how their actions lead to meaningful and lasting change. Traditional planning and evaluation tools often focus on activities and outputs while leaving underlying assumptions implicit. The Theory of Change framework emerged as a response to this limitation by offering a structured way to articulate causal pathways between interventions and desired outcomes. At a doctoral level of analysis, Theory of Change should be understood not merely as a planning tool but as a methodological approach to sense-making, learning, and accountability in complex systems.

title: HRM Practices in Government Companies of Bangladesh: A Case Study
affiliations: and Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB)

detail.title: HRM Practices in Government Companies of Bangladesh: A Case Study
detail.abstract: There is a paramount importance of Human Resource in a modern organization for its sustainability in future. Without the support of HR, machines remain idle, raw materials lie stacked, money get tied up, and other wings of the organization remain dysfunctional. Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited (TGTDCL) is the largest state-owned public limited gas company operating in the energy sector of Bangladesh under the Corporation of Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Resources (Petrobangla). This company is managed by the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources of Bangladesh. It is the most important and largest state-run company in terms of revenue earning, employment generation, and poverty alleviation of the country. Therefore, this study aims at evaluating the HRM systems of TGTDCL of Bangladesh. The study reveals that HRM systems of TGTDCL follow Bangladesh Service Rules (BSR) and unified service rules of Petrobangla. 'Service Regulations of TGTDCL 1987 and 2008' as well as 'Bangladesh Labor Law 2006' are used in this company. There is no unique HRM division as well as comprehensive HRM policy of this organization. The HR related activities are performed partially by the administrative, HRD and establishment departments. Study also shows that the HRM activities of TGTDCL are still traditional, backdated and not motivating to the skilled, brilliant and efficient employees of the company. There is formal Human Resource and Succession Planning. Although, the management has developed recently Titas Gas Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS) but it has not yet been implemented. The recruitment and selection process is standard but ineffective due to lengthy, irregular, and outdated implementation systems. Scattered informal and formal orientation programs are arranged for the newly recruited employees. Training is hardly based on Training Need Assessment (TNA). Although, the company arranges regular domestic and foreign training but there is hardly formal training policy of the company. The systematic promotion policy exists in the organization but not properly implemented due to the slow implementation process. Performance appraisal system is traditional and not motivating for the skilled employees. The benefits and other packages are as per government rules but far below the market standard. Fringe benefits are more than the other government employees. The grievance handling procedure is time consuming and often ineffective. Transfer, leave, and deputations are as per government rules. There is a good peer relation between the management and the trade union. Employees' welfare, safety and security measures are satisfactory compared to other government organizations. This study suggests that strategic HR planning, effective HRIS, formal job description should be developed thorough job analysis. Recruitment and selection process, Training Need Assessment, training manual, career planning, effective and updated promotion policy, performance appraisal systems, transfer, deputation, employee discipline and grievance handling procedures and employee welfare policies are to be improved by the policymakers to improve the productivity of this company.

title: Public Accountability of AI-Decision Support in Policing: Humans Blame the Victim, While Generative AI Blames the AI-Decision Support
affiliations: Vienna University of Economics and Business - Department of Management, Vienna University of Economics and Business, Leuphana University Lüneburg, Vienna University of Economics and Business, Vienna University of Economics and Business and University of Cincinnati

detail.title: Public Accountability of AI-Decision Support in Policing: Humans Blame the Victim, While Generative AI Blames the AI-Decision Support
detail.abstract: The increased use of (generative) AI in public services puts pressure on public accountability of decision-making, i.e., responsibility for decisions and their consequences could be attributed to the AI-decision support systems. Hence, questions on the ethicality of the decisions arise. We first use an experimental design to analyze the extent that people neutralize police violence. Second, we compare these results with answers from generative AI (ChatGPT). We assess whether neutralization happens as a result of (1) an AI advised arrest of a passerby, (2) the actual background of the passerby (i.e., whether the passerby had a criminal background or not, as verified by a post-hoc evaluation), and (3) the severity of the injury caused by a violent arrest. We find that both humans and generative AI attribute high importance to the actual background of the passerby (actual criminal or not) to classify behaviors as ethical or unethical. We find that humans do not neutralize police violence as a result of AI-decision support, while in 2 contrast, generative AI regularly and explicitly uses this as an argument to classify behavior as ethical or unethical.

title: Beyond Green Intentions - Gen'z Role in Sustainable Food Consumption for the Resilient Future
affiliations: , , ,  and

detail.title: Beyond Green Intentions - Gen'z Role in Sustainable Food Consumption for the Resilient Future
detail.abstract: Food wastage remains a major barrier to achieving Sustainable Development Goal 12, positioning Generation Z (Gen Z) as a critical demographic due to their heightened ecological consciousness, yet often contradictory consumption patterns (Schanes et al., 2018). Despite expressing strong pro-environmental attitudes, Gen Z frequently engages in impulsive buying influenced by emotional states and social-media-fueled consumer trends, contributing to increased waste (Stancu et al., 2016). Addressing an evident gap in existing scholarship, this research expands the Theory of Planned Behavior (Ajzen, 1991) by incorporating moral self-identity and perceived scarcity to more comprehensively assess Gen Z’s food-related decision-making. Anchored by two key inquiries—(1) the moderating role of moral identity and scarcity on the intention-behavior relationship, and (2) the influence of digital and financial literacy on waste-minimizing behaviors—a mixed-methods approach was utilized. Data included a survey of 412 urban Gen Z participants (aged 18–26) supported by 28 in-depth interviews, analyzed through structural equation modeling and thematic analysis. Results highlight that moral self-identity (β = 0.29, p < .01) and perceived scarcity (β = 0.22, p < .05) substantially enhance the translation of sustainable intentions into responsible actions. The findings suggest Gen Z adopts a “hybrid consumption behavior,” leveraging digital solutions (such as food-saving platforms) alongside four prominent practices: planned meals, deliberate purchasing, portion regulation, and innovative leftover utilization (Tarczyńska, 2021). Yet, trend-driven impulsive consumption enabled by digital media continues to undermine consistent progress (Visschers et al., 2016). The study asserts that although Gen Z’s personal commitment shows potential, broader systemic interventions are necessary. Strategic solutions including retail packaging redesign, community composting frameworks, and education that integrates both economic and environmental literacy are recommended to effectively reconcile Gen Z’s ethical aspirations with measurable food waste reduction.

title: Unheard Voices: Economic Challenges of Differently Abled Women in Kerala

detail.title: Unheard Voices: Economic Challenges of Differently Abled Women in Kerala
detail.abstract:
Differently abled women form one of the most oppressed and politically under-represented sections of the society. Even though Kerala performs best in various socio-economic and health indicators compared to other states of India, the status of women with disabilities is still in a pathetic condition. They face discrimination in every aspects of day-to-day life. Their physical and mental condition often marginalise them from the mainstream of society and development. Disability along with their low educational status make them unable to find their place in the job market. So, majority of them have to depend on their family members for their basic needs. This traps them in a cycle of economic vulnerability, yet their financial struggles often remain invisible within mainstream development discussions. This study seeks to uncover the economic challenges faced by differently abled women in Kerala, focusing specifically on how their expenditure patterns reflect deeper structural inequalities. Using primary data collected from 300 respondents, the research analyses economic status using variables like expenditure on food items and non-food items, particularly health, travel expenditure and miscellaneous expenditure. Economic impact may vary according to income, occupational status, and educational status. Also, it varies in accordance with the type of disability and bed-ridden status of the differently abled women.

The findings reveal that a disproportionate share of monthly expenditure is absorbed by medical treatment, mobility needs, and assistive equipment, leaving little room for savings or investments that could improve long-term financial security. Many respondents face recurring, unavoidable costs that exceed their earning capacity, contributing to chronic financial vulnerability. Positioned within the broader sustainability and inclusion agenda, the study underscores the need for policy interventions such as enhanced health subsidies, affordable assistive technologies, targeted social protection, and community-based support systems. By foregrounding the often-unheard economic experiences of differently abled women, this research contributes to a more inclusive understanding of sustainable development and offers practical insights for policymakers, welfare agencies, and gender-disability advocates.

title: AI Driven Supply Chain Management System
affiliations: Vishwakarma Institute of Technology, Vishwakarma Institute of Technology, Vishwakarma Institute of Technology, , Vishwakarma Institute of Technology, Vishwakarma Institute of Technology and

detail.title: AI Driven Supply Chain Management System
detail.abstract: Logistics are one of the most important aspects in the management of a business, it also contributes significantly in the expenses incurred by a business. A supply chain without proper logistics is prone to delays in every part of the production chain from manufacturing to retail. It is therefore imperative for a business to properly manage their logistics and supply chains for an efficient management of resources and maximization of profits. The current rise of Artificial Intelligence applications opens new horizons of expansion within logistics, thus streamlining this difficult process. This paper details a web application which utilizes artificial intelligence in order to assist businesses in “Supply Chain Management” and optimization. It is also capable of “Inventory Management” and “Demand Forecasting” which allows businesses to analyze their inventory and make decision to either keep it or sell it prematurely based on the circumstances. It can also ascertain which products are selling well and advise whether to buy stock or not. These allow businesses to save money and time in excess inventory and supply chain inefficiencies.

title: Beyond the Silicon Crunch: Sustainability and Resilience in Next-Generation Semiconductor Supply Chains
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Beyond the Silicon Crunch: Sustainability and Resilience in Next-Generation Semiconductor Supply Chains
detail.abstract: The semiconductor industry is entering a decade defined by intensifying environmental pressures, geopolitical fragmentation, and operational volatility. This study, positioned as a thought piece, argues that sustainability and resilience are no longer parallel priorities but deeply intertwined forces that shape the long-term stability of semiconductor supply chains. Drawing on emerging evidence and sectoral analysis, the study reframes the challenges facing the industry as systemic rather than isolated, driven by resource intensity, multi-tier opacity, demand amplification, and rising geopolitical constraints. It develops a forward-looking framework that explains how water and energy stewardship, circular material systems, collaborative governance, and digital transparency can simultaneously strengthen environmental performance and reduce exposure to disruption. The study then outlines a strategic blueprint for 2035 in which semiconductor networks operate through climate-aligned fabrication footprints, regenerative resource systems, intelligent redundancy, and multi-tier supplier development. By synthesizing these elements, the study shows that sustainability-led transformation is not a constraint but a pathway to operational continuity and competitive advantage. The analysis offers researchers, practitioners, and policymakers a cohesive vision for designing semiconductor supply chains that are transparent, adaptive, and environmentally responsible in an era of accelerating global uncertainty.

title: Personalizing Online Learning with AI: How Reputation mediates Learner Experience and Perception
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Personalizing Online Learning with AI: How Reputation mediates Learner Experience and Perception
detail.abstract: The EdTech sector is generously progressing and this study examines the impact of AI-based personalization on Learner Experience (LX), Learner Perception (LP) and EdTech platform reputation. The goal of this research is to explore the direct and indirect relationships between AI personalization and LX, perception and reputation and also evaluate the influence of EdTech reputation on LX, LP. A quantitative, descriptive research methodology was adopted, utilizing structures questionnaire administrated to 243 combining individual learners, students and professionals. Data analysis involved Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) to validate hypotheses and examine casual relationships. Findings revealed that AI-based personalization significantly enhances EdTech reputation and moderately improves LX, but does not directly influence LP. However, EdTech reputation emerged as a dominant factor significantly impacting both LX and LP. These outcomes emphasize that while AI-driven personalization enriches LX, a strong, credible platform reputation is crucial for shaping LP. Theoretically, this research bridges a critical gap by offering an integrated analytical framework connecting personalization, reputation and perception. Practically, it suggest that EdTech platform should invest not only in AI innovations but also in cultivating a sustainable brand reputation to maximize user satisfaction and loyalty. Future research should consider longitudinal studies and culturally diverse samples to deepen insights.

title: Driving Transformational Change: The Role of Employee Engagement in Organizational Success and Adaptability
affiliations: and

detail.title: Driving Transformational Change: The Role of Employee Engagement in Organizational Success and Adaptability
detail.abstract: This study focuses on transforming an organization that is increasingly driven by employee involvement, which is essential for integrating people into line with company objectives and cultivating an innovative and productive culture. In order to improve employee engagement and enable successful transformation, this research paper looks at elements like communication, coaching, training, job security, leadership, decision-making, feedback, reward and recognition. When combined, these components provide a thorough approach to improving the performance of organizations and also examine the organization's policies for implementing transformative change management, the researcher employs both primary and secondary to analyze the data and those collected information has been interpreted using one sample T test, which additionally aids the researcher to identify the conclusions and recommendations derived from the data gathered. Organizations may ensure long-term sustainability and competitive advantage in an increasingly dynamic business environment by incorporating these components into a coherent engagement strategy that not only improves employee satisfaction and retention but also drives effective change.

title: Propensity to Sacrifice Economic, Social, or Environmental Goals: Evidence from MSMEs in Haryana
affiliations: and

detail.title: Propensity to Sacrifice Economic, Social, or Environmental Goals: Evidence from MSMEs in Haryana
detail.abstract:
This study examines the propensity of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to sacrifice economic, social, or environmental goals when facing trade-offs. Although sustainability frameworks call for balance, MSMEs operate under tight resource limits that force prioritisation. Using primary survey data, this study identifies which sustainability dimension MSMEs are most likely to compromise under competitive pressure.

The analysis combines perceived importance, forced ranking of priorities, and responses to structured trade-off statements. This approach captures both stated views and revealed preferences. A composite sacrifice index is constructed to measure the relative propensity to sacrifice each sustainability dimension. Econometric models are then used to assess how business strategy, production type, and sustainability orientation shape sacrifice behaviour.

The findings reveal clear and consistent patterns in MSME decision-making under constraint. By focusing on propensity rather than intention, the study provides a more realistic account of sustainability trade-offs in MSMEs. The results offer policy-relevant insights for sustainability certification schemes and targeted support measures aimed at reducing systematic neglect of social and environmental goals.

title: Screening with Advertisements

detail.title: Screening with Advertisements
detail.abstract: We investigate a seller's revenue-maximizing mechanism in a setting where a desirable good is sold together with an undesirable bad (e.g., advertisements) that generates third-party revenue. The buyer's private information is two-dimensional: valuation for the good and willingness to pay to avoid the bad. Following the duality framework of Daskalakis, Deckelbaum, Tzamos (2017), whose results extend to our setting, we formulate the seller's problem using a transformed measure µ that depends on the third-party payment k. We provide a near-characterization for optimality of three pricing mechanisms commonly used in practice-the Good-Only, Ad-Tiered, and Single-Bundle Posted Prices-and introduce a new class of tractable, interpretable two-dimensional orthant conditions on µ for sufficiency. Economically, k yields a clean comparative static: low k excludes the bad, intermediate k separates ad-tolerant and ad-averse buyers, and high k bundles ads for all types.

title: Entrepreneurs and Credit Risk: A Machine Learning-Based Study on J&K Bank's Lending Portfolio
affiliations: and Lovely Professional University

detail.title: Entrepreneurs and Credit Risk: A Machine Learning-Based Study on J&K Bank's Lending Portfolio
detail.abstract: Credit Risk Assessment and Bankruptcy Prediction which is fundamental to Financial Stability define how banks deploy their Capital Allocation, Price Loans and Manage Portfolio Risk due to Economic Uncertainty). Advances in Machine Learning (ML), Artificial Intelligence (AI), allow for the application of High-Dimensional Financial, Behavioural, and Macroeconomic Data in order to model the Complex, Non-Linear Relationships between Credit Risk Factors which are often overlooked by Traditional Econometric Models. In this study we synthesize recent literature and applications regarding both the Econometric and Machine Learning approaches for Credit Risk Assessment and Bankruptcy Prediction and create a Hybrid Pipeline using both Methods on Primary Survey Data from 120 Entrepreneurs who had Bank Credit Relationships in a Regional Setting. Our Empirical Strategy consists of a combination of Data Cleaning, Saturated Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Regression, Factor Analysis and Decision Tree Classifier which classifies Loan Amount Categories as a Proxy for Credit Segmentation. The Factor Analysis recognizes three Latent Dimensions: Entrepreneurial and Managerial Capability, Financial Management and Credit Discipline, and Government Scheme Engagement, while the Decision Tree achieves roughly 72 percent Classification Accuracy and a Macro F1-Score of 0.71 on a Hold-Out Test Set. These findings demonstrate the additive advantages of both econometric and machine learning approaches, reveal the risks of overfitting in high-dimensional settings, and emphasize the importance of regularization, dimension reduction, and explainable AI when deploying machine learning-based credit risk and bankruptcy prediction models in practice.

detail.title: Enduring Terror: The Effects of the Boston Marathon Bombing on Competitive Performance
detail.abstract: The 2013 Boston Marathon Bombing was the largest domestic terrorist attack in the U.S. since the September 11 attacks. We ask how direct exposure to this terrorist attack influences performance and participation in future competitive environments. Our results indicate that exposed marathon runners suffer reductions in future performances both at Boston and at other major marathon events by approximately nine minutes. We find that these reductions in speed hinder runners' ability to qualify for future races, lowering participation among affected runners in subsequent Boston Marathons by nearly 10 percent. We also estimate persistent performance declines for finishers relative to runners who were not at the 2013 Marathon, contextualizing our main result as a lower bound. Finally, our findings are robust to a placebo test that assign a fictitious bombing to another marathon year, for which we find no comparable effects. Together, these results contribute to the growing literature on the direct effects of terrorism and underscore the need for long-term physical and mental health services, given the lasting and measurable impacts on victims.

publicationDetails.journalName: National Bank of Belgium Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper studies how employment subsidies for start-ups shape their performance. We exploit an unexpected policy reform in Belgium that permanently exempted start-ups hiring their first employee from payroll taxes for that employee. Using firm-level administrative data and a regression- discontinuity-in-time design, we find that subsidized post-reform start-ups employed fewer workers and generated lower output, value added, and profits compared to pre-reform start- ups. However, post-reform start-ups were more likely to survive as employers. These effects emerged within the first year after hiring and remained stable over a medium horizon of three years. Our findings indicate a compositional shift: the subsidy primarily induced low-productivity firms to enter the market. As most firms nowadays are nonemployers, our results meaningfully generalize the theoretical implications of standard neoclassical entrepreneurship models (employee–employer margin) and fill the important gap of the nonemployer–employer margin.

detail.abstract: Most discussion of AI in education focuses on remediation at the median. This paper argues that the largest long-run economic returns lie in using AI tutoring to accelerate the development of the top 0.51% of cognitively capable students. Because scientic breakthroughs are heavily concentrated among a narrow elite, even modest improvements in converting latent quantitative talent into frontier researchers can produce nonlinear returns to growth. Drawing on NSF doctoral production data and endogenous growth theory, we develop a recombination-based model in which the potential idea space scales combinatorially with elite researcher density. We then identify the geographic and socioeconomic frictions that currently suppress conversion of latent talent, and argue that AI tutoring is uniquely positioned to dissolve these local scarcity constraints. The mechanism is not replacing human mentorship but eliminating the binding constraint faced by high-ability students in low-resource environments: access to instruction, feedback, and intellectual challenge at the appropriate level.

detail.abstract:
This essay, built on keynote remarks, makes two claims. 

First, privacy, as a fundamental right, should be considered a principal component of data governance. In today’s world, the concerns about computer processing that arose in the 1960s and 1970s have accelerated even as policy remains behind. And where those concerns, and protections, in the United States have focused most closely on governmental collection and use of data, we now know that the porosity between commercial and government collection and use necessitates attention to both. Data governance thus must take into account, take seriously—and indeed, center—individual privacy.

Second, in the U.S., states have a key role to play in these efforts. Where federal efforts have fallen short, California and other states have picked up the privacy baton. Using as an illustrative example recent implementations of California’s Consumer Privacy Act by the California Privacy Protection Agency, the essay shows how fundamental rights concepts like autonomy are embedded within California’s updates to the “notice and choice” model.

States have always had an important role in privacy and data governance; today this role is crucial. The 2025 inauguration was quickly followed by actions that threaten to upend entirely the foundation of privacy and data protection that, at the federal level, has been in place since the 1970s, and in some cases approaching a century.  Indeed, federal activities today precisely echo the federal surveillance and harassment of Americans uncovered by the Church Committee in the 1970s.  State-level protections are vital to privacy, and to the democratic participation it enables.

detail.title: Value of Satisfied Marketing & Sales Employees for Customers and Shareholders
detail.abstract: Satisfied employees and satisfied customers are key to a firm's shareholder value. Surprisingly, prior research has provided inconclusive evidence on the associations among employee satisfaction, customer satisfaction, and shareholder value. Our interviews with 32 CEOs confirm this lack of clarity. Using an empirics-first approach and drawing on our CEO interviews, we develop a conceptual framework that offers conjectures about why the evidence may be mixed. Results from a large-scale dataset spanning 2013 to 2023 support the framework. Specifically, all four components of employee satisfaction-compensation and benefits, career opportunities, work-life balance, and culture and values-matter to marketing and sales employees, with culture and values and career opportunities as most consequential. Furthermore, marketing and sales employees' overall satisfaction is positively associated with customer satisfaction and negatively associated with customer dissatisfaction. However, it is customer satisfaction (and not customer dissatisfaction) that determines the firm's shareholder value. The research contributes to the literature at the intersection of employee satisfaction and customer satisfaction, and corrects managerial beliefs about pathways from marketing to shareholder value.

detail.abstract: As AI systems transition from experimental tools to integral components of organizational decision-making, discussions of AI governance have expanded rapidly across technical, operational, and administrative domains. However, contemporary practices often address governance concerns at different points in the AI lifecycle without clearly distinguishing their scope or limitations. This paper proposes a descriptive framework that identifies Four Stages of AI Governance: Model, Development, Deployment, and Operation. Rather than assessing maturity or effectiveness, this stage-based framing clarifies where governance mechanisms are applied and what aspects of AI systems they govern at each stage. In particular, the framework highlights the Development Stage as the phase in which decision formation structures and constraints are established-an area that has received comparatively less explicit attention amid increasing focus on deployment controls and runtime monitoring. By articulating these stages, this paper provides a neutral reference model for situating existing governance practices and emerging proposals within the broader AI lifecycle, without prescribing specific governance methodologies or standards.

detail.abstract: Revolving credit is at the core of the banking business. Corporate revolving credit lines are demandable claims; therefore, as with a traditional bank run on deposits, sudden widespread drawdowns on credit lines can destabilize the banking sector. However, we show that, unlike with deposits, credit-line utilization is highly sensitive to interest rates. A run on revolving lines is less likely in a high-interest-rate environment, but when the Federal Reserve cuts the interest rate to support a weak banking sector, the sector can become vulnerable to such a run.
